title: Shubman Gill Wins Record Fifth ICC Award as Shafali Verma Completes Double
excerpt: Gill's 110 and 223 against the West Indies earned him a fifth ICC Player of the Month award for September, while Verma's Asia Cup and Asian Games performances gave India both honours for a third time.
body:
• Shubman Gill won the ICC Men's Player of the Month award for September for a fifth time, extending his record in the men's category.
  • Gill scored 110 in the first ODI against the West Indies and 223 off 133 balls in the second, helping India chase 406.
  • Shafali Verma won the women's award for a second time after leading India's scoring at the Women's Asia Cup and starring at the Asian Games.
  • India swept both monthly awards for the third time, after similar doubles in June 2024 and September 2025.

India captain Shubman Gill has won the ICC Men's Player of the Month award for September, the governing body said, while opener Shafali Verma claimed the women's honour. The result gives India both awards for the month and extends Gill's record in the men's category to five wins.

Gill finished ahead of fellow India opener Abhishek Sharma and Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza on the men's shortlist, according to the Times of India report. Verma was chosen ahead of Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu and India spinner Sree Charani in the women's category. Both winners were decided by a vote of fans registered with the ICC and a panel of former internationals and media representatives.

A double-century that decided the month

Gill's case rested on two innings against the West Indies. In the opening one-day international in Thiruvananthapuram, he made 110 as India won by eight wickets to lead the series 1-0. In the next match, he scored 223 from 133 balls, described by the ICC as the quickest double-century in ODI history, as India chased a target of 406 and won by eight wickets with 39 balls remaining.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=fnAVqB0ToE4

"The result gives India both awards for the month and extends Gill's record in the men's category to five wins."

Gill said it felt "fantastic" to win a fifth time and thanked the panel, adding that contributing to successful chases in front of home supporters made the month more satisfying. He also pointed to the rising tempo of ODI cricket and to India's preparation for the men's World Cup in southern Africa next year, saying the team wants to keep raising its standards and build a balanced side.

His earlier monthly wins came in January and September 2023 and in February and July 2025. With five wins, he matches West Indies captain Hayley Matthews, who has also won the award five times across the men's and women's categories.

Verma's two-tournament run

Verma's award, her second, followed India's wins at the Women's Asia Cup and the Asian Games. The ICC said she was India's highest run-scorer at the Asia Cup, with 360 runs at a strike rate of 184.61, and that she also took six wickets in the period. At the Asian Games, she made an unbeaten 100 against Bangladesh in the semi-final and 48 in the final against Sri Lanka.

Verma said she was pleased to have played a part in both tournament wins and that the award made those results more special. She previously won the monthly award in November 2025 after her performance in the Women's World Cup final against South Africa in Navi Mumbai. Looking ahead, she cited the ICC Women's Champions Trophy in February next year as the next target.

Third sweep for India

The ICC said this was the fifth time players from the same board have won both awards in the same month and the third time India have done so. Jasprit Bumrah and Smriti Mandhana won in June 2024, while Abhishek Sharma and Mandhana won in September 2025.

For Gill, the award adds an individual marker to a series India controlled through its top order. For Verma, it confirms a return to decisive form in tournament finals and semi-finals. The next test for both is consistency: Gill in India's World Cup build-up in the ODI format, and Verma in a home Champions Trophy campaign where India will expect her early scoring to set the tone again.
